title: Career Roadmap— B.Sc. Nautical Science → Deck Cadet
summary: A Deck Cadet is a trainee officer in a ship's deck department who learns navigation, watchkeeping, cargo operations, ship safety, and maritime procedures under the supervision of qualified deck officers. It is a structured training stage toward becoming a certified deck officer and eventually a ship's captain.

blocks.text: A Deck Cadet is a trainee officer in a ship's deck department who learns navigation, watchkeeping, cargo operations, ship safety, and maritime procedures under the supervision of qualified deck officers. It is a structured training stage toward becoming a certified deck officer and eventually a ship's captain.

Unlike many other graduate careers, this pathway is governed by maritime regulations, approved training requirements, medical fitness standards, and certification rules. A B.Sc. Nautical Science degree alone does not automatically qualify someone to serve as a deck officer. The course, institution, sea-service training, examinations, and certificates must satisfy the applicable requirements of India's maritime administration and the relevant flag state.
What you will learn and do

items.text: Assist with bridge watchkeeping and navigation under supervision.
Learn chartwork, passage planning, and electronic navigation equipment.
Participate in ship safety drills and emergency preparedness.
Observe cargo handling, mooring, anchoring, and deck maintenance.
Maintain training records and complete required onboard competencies.
Learn maritime communication, teamwork, and international safety procedures.

blocks.text: Work environment
Merchant ships, cargo vessels, tankers, container ships, and other commercial vessels
Core strengths
Discipline, situational awareness, teamwork, resilience
Key requirements
Approved training, medical fitness, sea service, competency certification
Career direction
Before planning a deck-cadet career, confirm that the candidate's Nautical Science programme and training pathway are approved for the intended certification.
In India, the principal authority to consult is the Directorate General of Shipping (DGS).
The usual route involves:

items.text: Meeting the entry and medical requirements for the approved Nautical Science programme.
Completing the prescribed academic and practical training.
Obtaining required pre-sea safety and other mandatory training certificates.
Securing an eligible shipping-company placement for onboard training.
Completing the prescribed sea service and training record book requirements.
Passing the applicable competency examinations and completing any required post-sea training to progress toward officer certification.

blocks.label: Important
blocks.text: A deck-cadet berth is not guaranteed simply by enrolling in a college. Before paying admission fees, verify the institute's current approval, the exact programme, training arrangements, placement terms, and the requirements for obtaining a Certificate of Competency.

The standard B.Sc. Nautical Science pathway described by India's maritime administration comprises three years of campus training followed by prescribed onboard sea service. The exact sequence and sea-time requirements must be confirmed against the current approved programme and certification rules.
Directorate General of Shipping
Year 1
Foundations
Learn shipboard fundamentals

items.text: Study navigation, nautical mathematics, chartwork, and basic seamanship.
Learn ship construction, terminology, stability fundamentals, and maritime safety.
Practise compass use, knots, rope handling, and basic deck equipment procedures.
Develop maritime English, radio communication fundamentals, and teamwork.
Complete prescribed residential training, drills, and physical activities.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Demonstrate safe basic seamanship, understand bridge and deck terminology, and pass the required academic and practical assessments.
Year 2
Navigation
Develop navigational and operational knowledge

items.text: Study terrestrial and celestial navigation as prescribed by the syllabus.
Learn electronic navigation systems, including radar, ARPA, and ECDIS concepts.
Study meteorology, oceanography, tides, currents, and passage planning.
Learn cargo operations, ship stability, watchkeeping principles, and collision-prevention rules.
Practise emergency procedures, bridge communication, and structured training exercises.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Solve navigation and chartwork exercises, explain collision-avoidance principles, and understand how bridge teams maintain a safe navigational watch.
Year 3
Sea readiness
Prepare for onboard training

items.text: Consolidate navigation, ship stability, cargo work, maritime law, and safety.
Learn planned maintenance, mooring operations, anchoring, and deck inspections.
Complete required practical assessments and applicable pre-sea safety courses.
Prepare a professional maritime CV and apply through legitimate shipping-company cadet recruitment channels.
Understand the onboard training record book and how competencies are assessed.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Meet programme completion requirements, satisfy the required medical and documentation conditions, and secure an eligible sea-training berth.
Sea service
Onboard
Complete supervised shipboard training

items.text: Assist with bridge duties under the supervision of qualified officers.
Learn watchkeeping, passage planning, lookout procedures, and bridge equipment use.
Participate in cargo, deck maintenance, mooring, and emergency drills as assigned.
Complete the training record book and required onboard assessments.
Complete the applicable post-sea training and competency examinations.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Meet the prescribed sea-time, training, examination, and certification requirements to qualify for the next officer-certification stage. Do not assume that completing sea time alone grants an officer's licence.

rows.text: Charts, position fixing, passage planning, tides, and currents
Radar, ARPA, ECDIS, GNSS, compass systems
Knots, ropes, mooring, anchoring, deck equipment
Fire prevention, survival, first aid, emergency drills
Maritime English, bridge communication, applicable radio procedures
Discipline, teamwork, fatigue awareness, following orders

blocks.text: A cadet should learn these skills through approved instruction and supervised practice. Simulations and personal study are valuable supplements, not substitutes for mandatory training or authorization to operate shipboard equipment.
This is the most important section to verify before choosing this career.

For the Indian B.Sc. Nautical Science route, the published 2026–27 prospectus from the Indian Maritime University specifies academic and medical eligibility conditions. Requirements can differ by programme and applicant category, so consult the current admission documents rather than relying on a generic checklist.
IMU
Before enrolment, confirm:

blocks.label: Academic eligibility
blocks.text: Required Class 12 subjects and marks, including Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, and English, as applicable to the programme.

blocks.label: Age eligibility
blocks.text: The age limit and calculation date for the exact admission route.

blocks.label: Medical fitness
blocks.text: Examination by a doctor approved by the Directorate General of Shipping.

blocks.label: Eyesight and colour vision
blocks.text: Meet the current standards for the intended deck-officer pathway.

blocks.label: Training approval
blocks.text: Verify the institute and the exact B.Sc. Nautical Science course's current approval.

blocks.label: Sea-time and placement arrangements
blocks.text: Understand the onboard training requirements and how cadets obtain eligible berths.

blocks.label: Certification requirements
blocks.text: Confirm the steps to the Second Mate Certificate of Competency (CoC), including applicable examinations and post-sea training.
Do not rely solely on a college advertisement or an agent's verbal assurance. The DGS maintains official pages for approved maritime courses, institutes, training circulars, and related notices.

blocks.text: The exact requirements depend on the approved training route and the applicable maritime rules. Common training areas include:

rows.text: Safe conduct and working practices onboard
Security awareness or applicable ship-security training
Security responsibilities appropriate to the role
Confirms fitness under applicable maritime medical rules
Demonstrates the competence required for the relevant officer rank

blocks.text: Some modules may be integrated into an approved pre-sea programme. Confirm which certificates are required, when they must be completed, and whether they must be refreshed. Never assume an online certificate can replace a mandated practical course.

sections.heading: Internship, sea berth, and recruitment strategy

blocks.text: For this career, obtaining an eligible onboard training berth is a critical transition. Classroom performance matters, but a cadet also needs a valid pathway to complete sea service and competency requirements.
Where to investigate opportunities

items.text: Shipping companies with cadet recruitment or sponsorship programmes.
Training and placement offices at approved maritime institutes.
Merchant shipping companies operating container ships, bulk carriers, tankers, and other commercial vessels.
Official company career pages and legitimate maritime recruitment channels.

blocks.text: Examples of shipping organizations to research include Shipping Corporation of India, Great Eastern Shipping Company, and other established operators. This is a research list, not confirmation of current cadet openings or sponsorship.
Before accepting an offer, ask:

items.text: Is the training berth genuine and suitable for the required sea service?
What are the written sponsorship, placement, and training terms?
Who pays for travel, medical examinations, training, and documentation?
What happens if a berth is delayed or unavailable?
How will onboard training records and assessments be completed?
Does the route support the intended Certificate of Competency?

blocks.text: Be cautious about anyone guaranteeing a job or sea berth in exchange for an unexplained large payment. Verify recruiters and all contractual terms independently.
The deck department has a structured hierarchy. Advancement depends on the applicable sea service, examinations, competency certification, experience, and employer requirements.
Directorate General of Shipping

rows.text: Perform assigned navigation-watch and safety duties once certified
Commonly takes a significant role in passage planning and navigational responsibilities
Leads deck operations and cargo-related responsibilities
Overall command, safety, navigation, and operation of the vessel

blocks.text: These ranks are not automatic promotions. A cadet must meet the applicable certification and sea-service requirements at each stage.
Before committing, understand the realities of a seafaring career.

blocks.label: Time away from home
blocks.text: Contracts can involve extended periods at sea, with limited access to family and normal shore routines.

blocks.label: Shift work
blocks.text: Watchkeeping can require night shifts and irregular sleep schedules.

blocks.label: Safety responsibility
blocks.text: Procedures, drills, situational awareness, and compliance are essential.

blocks.label: Multicultural teamwork
blocks.text: Ships often have multinational crews and require clear professional communication.

blocks.label: Physical and mental demands
blocks.text: Candidates need to meet medical requirements and adapt to confined living and working conditions.

blocks.label: Career variability
blocks.text: Contract length, vessel type, employer, and time between assignments affect work and income.

The career may suit people who enjoy structured responsibility, navigation, technical learning, teamwork, and an international work environment. It may be less suitable for those who strongly prefer predictable daily schedules or frequent time at home.
Days 1–30
Verify
Check the approved programme, admission criteria, medical standards, eyesight requirements, and realistic sea-berth arrangements. Read the current IMU prospectus and DGS guidance.
Days 31–60
Prepare
Strengthen mathematics, physics, maritime English, navigation fundamentals, and basic seamanship knowledge. Prepare documents and investigate legitimate company recruitment or sponsorship routes.
Days 61–90
Plan the route

Compare approved institutions, written fees and placement terms, training facilities, and graduate outcomes. Confirm the certification sequence and create a financial plan for training and the transition to sea service.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: For a B.Sc. Nautical Science student in India, prioritize navigation, seamanship, safety, and disciplined practical training. Equally important, verify the approved education route, medical eligibility, and genuine onboard training arrangements. Your long-term objective is not simply to obtain a Deck Cadet title—it is to complete the required sea service and competency pathway toward becoming a qualified deck officer.
